data.gender_notes: Messiah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Messiah means 'Anointed One'. In the Christian faith, the Messiah is believed to be Jesus Christ, who was anointed by God to save humanity. The name Messiah carries the meaning “Anointed One, Savior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Messiah usually hope their child will grow to embody anointed one, savior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Messiah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Anointed One, Savior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Messiah total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: In the Jewish tradition, the Messiah is a future savior of the Jewish people. In Christianity, the term "Messiah" is used specifically to refer to Jesus Christ.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Messiah carries deep spiritual significance in both Judaism and Christianity, representing the hope for salvation and deliverance from sin and suffering. In Christianity, the belief in the Messiah as Jesus Christ is a core tenet of the faith, and the expectation of His return shapes the hope and anticipation of believers.
